newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgium's banks, Belgacom in chip card accord.
newsitem.headline: Belgium's banks, Belgacom in chip card accord.

text.p: Belgium's telephone operator Belgacom SA said on Friday it had agreed with the country's banking sector to introduce new chip-based payment products in 1997, including a combined bank, cash and calling card.

Baudouin Meunier, head of Belgacom's residential customers division, said the company would also pilot-test a new telephone set which would allow people to reload their bank chip cards with electronic cash and make payments from their homes.
Belgacom said it would begin to install new public telephone boxes capable of accepting the new combined cards from June. Ten thousand would be installed by June 1998.

Belgium's banks lead the world in the development of electronic money, having launched low-value, chip-based payment cards nationwide last May. The Belgian technology has also been sold to banks in the Netherlands, Switzerland, Australia and has also been licensed by American Express.
From January, the chip cards, marketed under the Proton brand, will be combined with the country's 18-year-old direct debit card payments network, Bancontact/Mister Cash.
Baudouin said the calling card function would give card holders the option of using electronic cash to pay for a call, or to have the call put on to their domestic telephone bill.
